items.title: Presentation: Modernising Retail at Scale: Architecting a Cloud-to-Edge Platform for a Global Enterprise (Source: feed.infoq.com)
items.content_text: Jayesh Bhayani discusses Tesco's decade-long enterprise transformation from fragmented legacy systems to a unified cloud-edge platform. He explains how aligning system, talent, and process modernizations allowed Tesco to scale mission-critical retail operations to millions of customers, while sharing practical lessons on build vs. buy, cloud cost management, and preparing for agentic commerce. By Jayesh Bhayani

items.title: EA modeling tools: how do you choose the right one? (Source: www.leanix.net)
items.content_text: EA programs don't fail because of notation depth, but lack of data quality and adoption. Discover the right metrics for choosing a modeling tool.

items.title: Article: Governed Autonomous Intelligence for Mission-Critical Utility (Source: feed.infoq.com)
items.content_text: The article describes an architecture for agentic AI in regulated utility operations. Agents reason and propose actions, but a deterministic policy gate and a governed tool gateway control execution, with human approval where required. It covers an AWS reference implementation, grounding in runbooks, governed prediction, outcome validation, audit evidence, and phased autonomy. By Purnang Borah

items.title: Presentation: Opening the Black Box: Critical Explainability for AI Agent Tool Selection with Kiji Inspector (Source: feed.infoq.com)
items.content_text: Hannes Hapke shares how Dataiku's open-source Kiji Inspector applies Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) directly to decision tokens to expose why agents pick specific tools. Moving past superficial chain-of-thought narratives, he discusses causal ablation, layer activation extraction via patched vLLM engines, and production monitoring workflows for software architects and senior engineering leaders. By Hannes Hapke

items.content_text: Enterprise AI is gaining the context and authority to do real work, not just generate answers. As autonomy grows, CIOs must balance business value with governance, portability, and control.
